_what: Differences between an origin project's own guard scripts and the kit's ported ones that the extraction MEANT to introduce. Each entry is signed for: it says why the two versions SHOULD differ. dual_run prints them, and still fails on any difference not listed.
_why_not_code: These entries name a specific film's filenames, and the kit's own lint refuses a project noun in code. This is data about one comparison, so it lives in a file — the same treatment preflight's fixture corpus got.
_do_not: Do not add an entry to turn a red run green. Add one when you can say, in a sentence, why the two versions should differ.

differences.to_means: null = substitute the film's own facts filename
differences.why: FK1 removed a hard-coded project filename from lint_prompt's direction-audit message, so it now names whichever facts file the film actually uses. The origin says tarn_facts.json because that is the only film it could ever describe.

_two_kinds: `differences` are TEXT substitutions: the same work reported in different words. `divergences` are BEHAVIOUR: the kit deliberately doing more or less than the origin. The second kind cannot be expressed as a substitution and must never be smuggled in as one — it narrows what the acceptance run proves, and the report says so by name.

divergences.why: The film declared its `prompts` role as FOUR ledgers. The origin's staleness hard-codes one of them, so three were never checked for a superseded block calling itself live. The kit reads all four, and also checks LIVE-role uniqueness ACROSS ledgers, which the origin could not do at all. The outputs therefore differ by design, and the origin's is the smaller of the two.
divergences.narrows: staleness.py is no longer evidence that the extraction changed nothing. It is evidence of a change somebody asked for. Every other invocation still carries the original claim.

divergences.why: preflight RUNS staleness and prints its report, so it inherits the widened prompts role. Nothing in preflight itself changed.
divergences.narrows: This is the expensive one. preflight is the largest tool in the kit and excluding it removes most of what a single acceptance run covers. The extraction evidence for this film is the run made at ADOPTION time, with the prompts role declared as the single ledger the origin read: 43 invocations, all agreeing. Keep that run. This one answers a different question — what widening the role changed — and answers it well.

divergences.why: FK-26. The kit's staleness reads the BODY of every LIVE block and refuses one that names a conditioning frame which is not the current selection for that role. The origin's does not — it asks whether a WITHDRAWN selection is labelled withdrawn, and stops there, so the prompt block, which is the artefact that actually gets pasted into the UI with two filenames in its first line, was checked by nothing. Measured on the origin film on 6 Aug: a LIVE 54-credit block still naming a start_image and an end_image that had both been superseded on 31 Jul, quoting a frames_check --pair reading taken on the dead pair, at 0 linter errors.
divergences.narrows: Nothing at all on a film that keeps no selections — the check is silent and the comparison stays exact. On a film that keeps them, staleness stops being evidence that the extraction changed nothing and becomes evidence of a check the origin never had. The origin's output is the smaller of the two, and its silence is the finding rather than the baseline.

divergences.why: FK-26 again: preflight RUNS staleness and prints its report, so it inherits the frame-reference check. Nothing in preflight itself changed. Listed as its own entry rather than folded into the prompts-role one above, because it is a separate cause and an exemption signed for one reason must never quietly cover another.
divergences.narrows: As staleness above, multiplied by preflight being the largest tool in the kit. The extraction evidence for this film remains the adoption run — 43 invocations, all agreeing. This run answers a different question: what the new check changed.

_when: A divergence is in force ONLY while its stated cause is. `when` names the condition -- either a file role declared as several files, or a top-level facts key being present. Without it the entry would excuse that tool from the comparison forever, and a real change would land inside an exemption somebody signed for a different reason.
_several_per_tool: One tool may appear several times with different `when` conditions. dual_run groups them by tool and prints every one that is in force, and names the CAUSE of each dormant entry rather than the bare tool name -- a tool can be divergent for one reason and dormant for another in the same run.
